title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of E420 (Novi Commentarii Acad. Sci. Petropolitanae 16, published 1772). Euler sets up the objects whose variations he will compute.

§1: If y is any function of x, then every expression built from x and y can be regarded as a function of the single variable x. It takes a definite value for each value of x.

§2: Such expressions fall into three kinds (genera).
- Genus I: point functions F(x,y), built by algebraic or transcendental operations. Examples are αx^3+βxy+γy^3 and e^{αx}·arcsin y.
- Genus II (begun on this page, continued on the next): expressions that also contain differential ratios. Writing dy = p dx, dp = q dx, etc., these are functions F(x,y,p,q,r,...), i.e. functions on the jet space.
- Genus III (next page): expressions containing integral formulas ∫V dx. Here V depends on x, y, p, q, ... and may itself contain further integrals.

The purpose is to prepare the problem of §3 and later sections: find the change in all three kinds of expression when the relation y(x) is varied infinitesimally. In the paper's sequel Euler introduces an auxiliary parameter, so that δ becomes partial differentiation with respect to that parameter. That is the familiar one-parameter-family form of the variational derivative. On this page itself there is only the classification and the motivating setup.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor uncertainty: the scan's exponents in the example αx^3+βxy+γy^3 are hard to read; they may be 2 (which would give a homogeneous quadratic). This does not affect anything.

ideas.what: Viewing all expressions in x, y as functions of x once y=y(x) is fixed
ideas.modern_name: composition / pullback along a section y(x)
ideas.where_published: E420; also E385 Elementa calculi variationum and Institutiones calculi integralis vol. 3 appendix

ideas.what: Threefold classification: point functions, functions of derivatives p,q,r..., integral functionals ∫V dx (possibly nested)
ideas.modern_name: functions on the base, functions on jet space, (nested) integral functionals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Elementa calculi variationum, E296; E420); Lagrange's δ-method as background
ideas.where_published: E296 Elementa calculi variationum (1766), E297, E420; Inst. calc. int. III (E385) supplement

deep.surprise_reason: This is an introductory, classificatory page whose content is well documented in histories of the calculus of variations (e.g. Goldstine, Fraser). The paper's known contribution, the parameter interpretation of δ, is not yet on this page.
transcription_corrections: Header: the '[?]' can be dropped. The page shows a centred ornamented '( 35 )' (Novi Comm. 16, p. 35), possibly with a duplicated page number at the right edge.
The exponents in 'αx^{3}+βxy+γy^{3}' are uncertain in the scan (could be squares); they should be verified against a clean copy.
Neighbouring-page header '382' is presumably a misreading of '36'.
